top_choice_rationale: P001 gives the cleanest allocation on the slate: Katori and Ye, with a citation built on the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock rather than on the comb or single-ion control, and with 1e-18 performance independently confirmed, so maturity is settled. Six of eight members back it with the same pair. I accept the objection that it honours a measurement invention in territory already recognised in 2005 and 2012, but the many-atom lattice regime is a distinct physical step and the clocks now serve as instruments for fundamental physics. P002 (twisted bilayer graphene) is the more field-creating subject but remains less mature, with unresolved superconductivity and incomplete credit (Cao, Fatemi, the hBN moire groups), so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
